items.title: Tom Albert Interview, 1962-05-07
items.q: Sometimes I used to go to Louis Domaine. Louis Domaine used to get them, I used to buy them. He used to go and copy them off of me.

ctx.x: They were harder than hanging out.

Yeah, harder than hanging out. But the most thing we used to get those piano covers, and we'd copy off of them. Sometimes I used to go to Louis Domaine. Louis Domaine used to get them, I used to buy them. He used to go and copy them off of me. And I'd copy the trombone part and the cornet part. That's all we need. I'd like to get one piece, that's all. If I get one, if I get a piece of copy, that's all I need. And then I'd play to the fellow, he'd catch it. And he'd hear it and play. That's all. We were high…
Well, when you first moved here from Algiers, did you, well, let's see, you say you moved from Sox's Lane to Dublin? Dublin.
